finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: If the input exceeds MAX_LINE_LENGTH, it could lead to a buffer overflow.
finding.assumptions: The input is not limited to MAX_LINE_LENGTH and could potentially exceed it.

parsed.change_summary: No changes were made to the code as the reported vulnerability is not present in the provided code fragment. The code already ensures that the input is limited to MAX_LINE_LENGTH and does not exceed it.
parsed.how_trigger_is_blocked: The trigger described in the finding no longer works because the code already includes a check to ensure that the input is limited to MAX_LINE_LENGTH. The loop in the get_line function only reads up to max - 1 characters, and any additional characters are ignored. Therefore, even if the input exceeds MAX_LINE_LENGTH, it will not lead to a buffer overflow.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the loop bounds in get_line: the condition i < max - 1 guarantees that at most max-1 characters are stored. After the loop, if a newline is read, it is stored and i is incremented, but i can only reach max-1, so the null terminator written at line[i] is within bounds. No unchecked copy or overflow can occur. No other code paths allow writing beyond the array. The patch is identical to the original code, so it does not change behavior.
